The rep held setter scope cleanly on financing/battery questions and stayed disciplined through the bill-collection and credit-qualifier sections, though the wife-as-co-owner is identified but never explicitly invited onto the appointment.

observed_outcome.reasoning: Customer begins to answer with a time preference and the rep supplies 'five ish' which the customer confirms works — day (Tuesday) and time (5pm) are both locked, and the format is in-person per the rep's earlier hold of that policy at 08:18. The wife, identified as co-owner at 04:23, is never explicitly confirmed for this appointment.

primary_coaching_focus.why: The wife is identified as a title co-owner but is never explicitly invited or confirmed for the Tuesday 5pm visit — the customer's own later comment about 'automated schedules' making it hard to get them both home at once suggests this appointment may proceed without her, which risks a stalled close per protocols.spouse_decision.

key_moments.quote: I've heard both both stories. So what got what got me, what caught my attention under your ad is, it says solar, no cost, and you get a, Tesla Powerwall, and stuff like that.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer discloses he already has quotes from multiple companies AND cites a specific ad promise (free Powerwall). The rep never asks which companies or what those competitors offered, losing competitive intel the closer could use.

key_moments.quote: it says solar, no cost, and you get a, Tesla Powerwall, and stuff like that.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer is anchored on a specific marketed promise — a free Powerwall — which is a real Ion offering (the only battery brand Ion carries) but nothing in the call confirms or scopes that expectation for the closer. The rep's later deferral at 02:00 addresses PPA vs. purchase generally but never separately flags the battery expectation as its own line item.

key_moments.quote: I I like paying for what I consume, and I guess whatever, you know, delivery fee they're charging should be included already in the rate that you're selling them exclusively at.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer is talking himself through whether solar will actually lower his bill, given that delivery fees (not usage) drive his cost — this is exactly the moment to flip the fixed-fee pain into a reason solar still helps usage-based charges, but the rep says nothing and lets the customer keep reasoning out loud alone.

key_moments.quote: But I'm not interested in the PPA at all. That's that's just like, you can put that in the notes as well.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is a stated financing-structure preference, not a cost/time/interest objection — the customer isn't objecting to solar, he's pre-filtering which offer structure he'll accept. The rep correctly logs it for the notes rather than trying to talk him out of his preference.
